title: Ex-Marineland beluga whale dies in Chicago aquarium
summary: Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga, died on Wednesday, becoming the sixth animal from the closed Ontario theme park Marineland to die after a massive relocation of…

image.caption: Visitors look at beluga whales at the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago in November 2012. The aquarium says Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga relocated from now-defunct Ontario-based Marineland, died on Wednesday despite efforts to save her. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga, died on Wednesday, becoming the sixth animal from the closed Ontario theme park Marineland to die after a massive relocation of whales and dolphins over the summer.
4 other belugas, 1 dolphin have also died after relocation from closed Canadian theme park
Another whale shipped out of Marineland has died at the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago.
The aquarium says Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga, died on Wednesday despite efforts to save her.
It's the sixth animal from the closed Niagara Falls, Ont., theme park to die after a massive relocation of whales and dolphins over the summer.
Four other belugas and one dolphin from Marineland have died since they were moved out of the former tourist attraction.

items: 4 Marineland belugas, 1 dolphin, died after being transferred. Why the rest remain on 'death watch'
'Emergency rescue' of Marineland's beluga whales to U.S. aquariums has begun

blocks.text: Shedd says Caspian had not been eating properly and blood samples showed abnormalities in her electrolyte levels. The park added that her blood had become "dangerously acidic."
The aquarium says those findings helped the veterinary care team understand how sick the beluga was, but they did not establish a cause of death.
Shedd says Caspian was on life support for nearly four hours before she died.
Why Marineland's last living belugas are on 'death watch'
Shedd recently performed necropsies on Peekachu and Rain, two other Marineland whales that died there, and concluded that they had chronic, pre-existing diseases.
Shedd and four other aquariums in the United States and Spain helped Marineland relocate all 30 of its belugas and four dolphins over the course of six weeks this summer.
Marineland had said it was running out of money and could no longer care for the last captive whales and dolphins in Canada.
A beluga named Jelly Bean and a dolphin named Echo died at Oceanografic Valencia in Spain after the move.
